questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

“Cheer up, father, I’ll go and get work somewhere.” said Jane.

options.text: Jane ask her father to cheer up as she will go and get work somewhere.
Jane asked her father to cheer up, because she would be gone and got work somewhere.
Jane asks her father to cheer up as she would get job.
Jane asked her father to cheer up as she would go and get work somewhere.

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Jane asked her father to cheer up as she would go and get work somewhere**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **simple future tense (***will go*).
 
• In the indirect speech, '**will'*** *changes to '**would'**.
 
• Let's look at the steps for changing the sentence from direct to indirect speech:
 
 
• As the reporting verb is in the** past tense** and direct speech is in the **simple future tense**, we will take the following steps:-
 
• The reporting verb** 'said' **is changed to** 'asked' **because the girl is asking her father to cheer up.
 
• The conjunction 'that' is used in place of the comma and the inverted comma are removed.
 
• The pronoun 'I' is changed to 'she' as the first person changes according to subject.
 
 

**Therefore, the correct indirect speech is ***Jane asked her father to cheer up as she would go and get work somewhere.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Shah Jahan built the Red Fort.

options.text: The Red Fort is build by Shah Jahan.
The Red Fort was built by Shah Jahan.
The Red Fort got build by Shah Jahan.
The Red Fort built by Shah Jahan.

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **The Red Fort was built by Shah Jahan.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

__
 
• The given sentence**(active voice) **is in the **simple past tense (built)*. ***
 
• The passive voice will be:- 
 
• **was/were + past participle of build(built) + by.**
 
• Whenever an active voice is in simple past tense, it is changed into passive voice according to the following structure:-
 
 
• Active Voice - **did+ V₁ or V₂**
 
• Passive voice - **was/were + V₃**
 
 
 
• **For Example:-**
 
 
• Active Voice - Shah Jahan built the Moti Masjid.
 
• Passive Voice - Moti Masjid was built by Shah Jahan.
 
 

**Therefore, the correct passive voice of the given active voice is ***The Red Fort was built by Shah Jahan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• When we convert active voice to passive voice, three things need to be kept in mind:-

 
 
• Change object into subject.
 
• Change subject into object.
 
• Always use third form of verb in passive voice.
 
• Use 'by' before the new object.

**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

You’ll spend most of your time gaping (1)/ in awe at the Kailash temple, but that (2)/ isn’t a only gem that Ellora has to offer. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-
__
 
• In the above given sentence, the error is in **part 3**.
 
• It is so because 'a' will be replaced by** 'the'**.
 
• **'Only gem'** indicates that the given noun is special and unique** i.e. it is definite.**
 
• Thus, the definite article i.e.** 'the'** will be used in place of the indefinite article i.e. **'a'.** 
 
• Definite article 'the' is used **when the noun with which it is used is a particular one, which is identifiable to the listener.**
 
• It may also be used for a noun that has already been mentioned or is uniquely specified.
 
 
• For Example - This is** the **girl who sings.
 
 
 
• In the above sentence, **the girl has been specified to be the one who sings.**
 
• Thus,** 'a'** will be replaced by **'the'**.

**Therefore, the correct sentence is*** You’ll spend most of your time gaping in awe at the Kailash temple, but that isn’t the only gem that Ellora has to offer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• **Indefinite articles** i.e. **'a' **and **'an' **are used** to introduce new concepts(noun phrase) into a discourse.**
 
• These articles are called indefinite because **their usage implies that the thing which is being referred to is nonspecific.**
 
• For Example - He caught** a** bird.**(any bird)**
 
• **Note **- Indefinite articles are generally used before countable 'singular' nouns.

questions.question: In Indian Parliament, under which condition a house can declare the seat of a member vacant?

If member is absent from all meetings of the house for 45 days continuously
If member is absent from all meetings of the house for 30 days continuously
If member is absent from all meetings of the house for 21 days continuously

questions.solution:
• If member is absent from all meetings of the house for 60 days continuously, a house can declare the seat of a member vacant.
 
• Article 101 of the Constitution of India deals with disqualification of members. It lays down several ways in which the seat may become vacant.
 
• Article 101 (4) provides that the House may declare the seat vacant if the member is absent for a period of sixty days, not counting any period when the House is prorogued or adjourned for four or more consecutive days.

• If the court declares his Election as void.
 
• If the house expels him.

questions.question: There are usually three Parliamentary sessions in India, viz, the Budget session, the Monsoon session, and _______.
questions.solution:
There are usually three Parliamentary sessions in India, viz, the Budget session, the Monsoon session,and the Winter session.

The period during which the Houses - Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha - meet to conduct its business, is called session.

There are three types of Sessions that are conducted in the Parliament of India:

 
• Budget session: from February to May.
 
• Monsoon session: from July to September.
 
• Winter session: from November to December.

The Constitution empowers the president to summon each House at such intervals that there should not be more than a six-month gap between the two sessions.
